notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
There has been a bit of a pause in both the communication and the development of the game, as I am sure most if not all of you reading this will know. There are three things I need to tell you.

First off, the company, Scion Studios, was about to run out of cash before the summer. That had to be solved, and it has. Part time contracting work has put us in a much healthier position. If the company folds there will be no game.

Secondly, the cash issue led to another issue; A mad dash to profitability, code quality be damned. Over time this built up and made the code... less than ideal to work with.
Over the past month a truly massive amount of work has been spent on paying off all the technical debt the project had accrued. We're talking in the tens of thousands of changes.
From a technical point of view, the project is in a great state now.

Third and perhaps most importantly, I don't know about you guys but I was always somewhat disappointed by how poorly the game came together. The mechanics feel like they are somewhat fighting each other instead of elevating each other. This last point has been the one causing me the most both heartache and headache. I realized I was out of my depth and that I need help. A few months of daring to venture outside the development-basement I have now made a few new friends, two of which happen to be world class game designers. Over the coming weeks I am going to be putting together the grand master plan for how to finally achieve greatness. 

The starting point for the grand master plan is this;
A Game of Humans is fundamentally about humans. There is a deep simulation going on and things happening, yet it matters little to the actual running of the city/game except for productivity.
I am moving the game towards something where the goal is to expand and attract more people, but more people will only come if the existing ones are happy. To make the existing people happy you have to deal with the drama they generate (new mechanic), applying faith powers and sometimes choosing the lesser of two evils. It is likely that the way feelings work will change, into a much more interactive mechanic.

What do you think would make this game better?

(and sorry about the news hiatus, in-between pushing myself too hard and running out of cash, it turns out I managed to burn myself out. It's been a life lesson)

notes.title: The Peoples Patch (0.3) Live Now
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/1e6d064797d6a8bfae8358f3a3742941637b6b75.png[/img]


Patch 0.3 is now available. This patch took longer than expected. In addition to all the public facing features, a ton of internals were updated. We are now moving to a monthly release schedule, with more frequent smaller patches.

There is now an official Discord server, the link to which you will find in the game.
Please note that the most requested feature by far at this point is more plot types, something which will be addressed in the next patch.

Please let us know what you think and what you most would like to see added in the future.
Now, on to the changes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/271f19b8212e7bb34d00e3ba7021d896904a9643.png[/img]
[i]A model citizen[/i]

[h3]Overhauled character model[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Needs[/b]
- Sleep
- Thirst
- Energy
- Nature
- Hunger
[*][b]Desires[/b]
- Work
- Social
- Spiritual
[*][b]Attributes[/b]
- Beauty
- Strength
- Endurance
- Intelligence
[*][b]Personality[/b]
- Curious
- Friendly
- Extrovert
- Sensitive
- Productive
[*][b]Traits[/b]
- Over 60 traits with unique effects
- Generated by personality
- Example: A character can become Immature if they have are low in curious and productive. Immature people have -20 likeability effect.
[*][b]Feelings[/b]
- Mood
- Happiness
[*][b]Thoughts[/b]
- Triggered by certain events or just by existing
- Effects on moods and relations
[*][b]Skills[/b]
- The more a character does something the better the person is at it
- Currently 7 skills, more to come
[*][b]Relations[/b]
- Characters now have a GUI tab where you can see a characters relations
- Characters can now became friends or foes
[*][b]Stats[/b]
- A collection of values that affect the characters
- Movement speed
- Learning speed
- Strength activities
- Intellectual activities
- Liking
- Likeability
- Laughter chance
- Argument chance
- Meeting new people
- Energy expenditure
- Positive feelings
- Negative feelings
[*][b]Records[/b]
- A record of things that character has done
- Arrival day
- Worked hours
- Acquaintances
- Friends
- Foes
- Conversations
- Laughs
- Arguments
[*][b]Beliefs & Prophets[/b]
- When accruing faith, the player will trigger the formation of beliefs
- A belief is a set of values
- 7 traits are selected to be vices and 7 to be virtues
- When someone holding a belief is talking to another person, they have a chance to transmit their belief to them
- Chances of this happening increases greatly the more virtues the person has, the less vices and what they think of the person they are talking to
[*][b]Voices[/b]
- All characters now speak gibberish
[/list]
[h3]New god power system[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Divine Toot[/b]
- When least expected, the gods play tricks on the innocent
[*][b]Divine Vision[/b]
- Messages from the gods are known to sometimes cause prophetical beliefs
[*][b]Heavenly Food[/b]
- At times the gods may feel the need to stave off starvation
[*][b]Heavenly Water[/b]
- The purest of water straight from the divine spring itself
[*][b]Heavenly Treasure[/b]
- Some people deserve money more than others
[*][b]Joviality[/b]
- A feeling of pure joy. All conversations will be happy ones
[*][b]Morosity[/b]
- An abhorrent feeling of chaos. All conversations will be angry ones
[*][b]Insomnia[/b]
- There are times when people simply cant sleep
[*][b]Sense of Urgency[/b]
- Sometimes people need a little sense of urgency in their lives
[/list]

[*][b]Carpentry[/b]
- Can now create furniture that is then sold to plots and assembled
[*][b]Forestry[/b]
- Now cuts down and replants trees instead of just collecting wood and selling

notes.title: Peoples Patch (0.3) Beta Available Now
notes.content:
Hi everyone and thank you for taking the time to read this.

First things first, patch 0.3 is nearing completion and is now available for public testing. In order to partake, please right click on "A Game of Humans" in your Steam library, select the "Properties..." menu and then go to the "Beta" tab.

Come to think of it, I am not entirely sure how clearly the goal of the project was stated when we first went live. So let me do that now; [b]The goal of A Game of Humans is to create the deepest possible colony simulator and god game hybrid.[/b] 
Depth sounds nice and all, but what does it mean? The character rework in this patch is the first answer to that question.

[h2]What's in this patch?[/h2]
The official name of this patch is "The Peoples Patch". The goal was to take what we had in 0.2 and do two things; solidify the gameplay systems so the rest of the game can be built on top of it and deepen the character simulation so we could start approaching what has been the goal all along, characters that feel as alive as a character in The Sims. 

The meat of this patch consists primarily of two things;
[list]
[*]Character rework
[*]Information display (it should now be[i] a lot [/i]easier to understand what is going on)
[/list]
Characters now have;
[list]
[*]Traits
[*]Personalities
[*]Voices
[*]Thoughts
[*]Skills
[*]Stats
[*]Records
[*]Relations
[*]Inventory (though more items still need to be added, such as clothing made by tailors)
[/list]
This patch also adds the foundation of the economic gameplay, namely supply & demand based price fluctuation. This is going to come into more effect as off map traders and taverns are added.

The new personality system allows us to simulate things way beyond what could be done before. Look at this fellow for example, Orvaldur. A friendly and social guy, but not very organized nor intelligent. This is reflected by the stats, derived from the personality. Orvaldur will never be an expert at what he does, but he will be liked by most others. Unfortunately, this also means Orvaldur will be easily fooled by others (this is where the future crime update will come in, the feature I am perhaps most excited about)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/5bc93c200f67204b6d825d507a30aa2043a09f92.png[/img]

[h2]Why did it take so long?[/h2]
Patch 0.2 was essentially a bunch fixes and small changes. Patch 0.3 was going to be the next step in the evolution of the game. As we began the implementation we slowly came to the realization that we had more work to do than we originally estimated. An estimate of 6 months turned into twice that. 
I now understand why the game we set out to make has not yet been made, turns out the AI is really tricky to get right. The AI present in the previous versions (including the character model that drove the AI behavior) simply wasn't up to scruff, it didn't produce the depth we needed it to.

[h2]What's happening now?[/h2]
From this point on patches are going to be smaller and a lot more frequent.
If you download the beta, you will notice that the faith powers are gone for now. They are going to be making a grand re-entry before the official release of patch 0.3. The faith/god powers are where the meat of the gameplay experience is going to be. The intention is to build a system that rewards the player for paying attention to the simulation, manipulating the behavior of the Humans to produce the perfect village.

notes.title: Small Update + Teaser
notes.content:
It has been a while since the last news update. The primary reason for this is my procilivity for postponing things until they can be done properly. I shamefully admit it took way too long until it occured to me that it is as a matter of fact possible to write a small update while working on the major ones.

So what's going on with the game and where are we heading.

Version 0.1 released in June 2020. The feedback this generated has been immeasurably useful. It helped align the game design and production plan towards what matters. It allowed us to track down and fix a couple very hard to find tech issues (nerd alert; raunchy race conditions). Your feedback and reviews also gave us the confidence to start another investment round and it gave our investors faith in the long term success of the project. I don't want to jinx it, but the likelihood of us pulling a Titanic on our maiden voyage has been greatly reduced (though, in all fairness, that is what the Titanic thought as well).

Version 0.2 released in October 2020. It addressed three things; onboarding, information presentation and the above mentioned tech issues. Not the most exciting features but definitely required before we could work on the more exciting stuff.

Version 0.3 has been in the works ever since. It was the first time in almost a year where we could sit down and reasonably ask ourselves; alright, out of all the stuff we want in the final product that isn't in yet, what do we prioritize?

There is going to be a lot of information between now and the release of patch 0.3, where we will be diving deeper into all the changes. 
For now, here's the promised teaser. 
Old character to the left, new character to the right. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/d47183593c5fcf7669011ab53c465a27e4770c22.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/ec02ff5be4296ea551ef6377dd8ec16aafec0745.png[/img][/url]

Wishlist us and stay tuned for more!
/August

notes.title: Patch 0.2 now available
notes.content:
[h3]The first major patch for a A Game of Humans is finally here. A big thank you goes out to all those of you who have participated. Your feedback has been invaluable.[/h3] 


[b]Game log[/b]
The game log displays messages for the player in the lower right part of the screen. This is used for everything from announcements to tutorial messages.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/6c89b68fb4f581c7e1cadbf45849be1bd0811898.png[/img]

[b]Floating text[/b]
A system has been added that allows for the displaying of information above characters. This is used liberally to display what is going on in your citizens lives such.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/a64b1ada71a1df2b00cfc5236e5cc3e028d9a154.png[/img]

[b]Women[/b]
The ruggedness of the male settlers appear to have attracted females.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/53245aa166282eabda12bfc9d11d03ececfdcc5e.png[/img]

[b]Opinions[/b]
Characters form a limited amount of relationships with others. Extroverts will have more relationships that introverts (relationship as is knows of, not the romantic version). How well they get along depends on their personalities.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/c6b8ff5a1a8b90ba38fcf0e8f36b0e84037482dd.png[/img]

[b]Political views[/b]
Based on their personalities people will believe in different things and vote accordingly.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/73b6b543daa528ce5c7999606faefcffc0731a20.png[/img]

[b]Townhall[/b]
Once a townhall plot has been placed and a building has been constructed on it you can hold elections by placing a ballot box in the townhall.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/c5e56645db29d7ec01602e2987f7cb79ac9afd18.png[/img]

[b]Mayor[/b]
The Mayor forms the backbone of the administration, settings laws and hiring tax collectors.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/5cfdec9050cacb911fc4dc28d8510cb11ed26ba1.png[/img]

[b]Elections[/b]
People discuss and vote for their favorite candidates. When deciding they care about their opinion of the candidate, the candidates popularity, similarity of political views (laws) and people are less likely to vote for the current Mayor if they are unhappy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/20f11307cdfff72bc7031df6437285b04ffb9129.png[/img]

[b]Laws[/b]
The Mayor sets the laws and there are currently two of them; Working hours law (labor laws) and tax rates. The Mayor sets them according to his/her political views.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/3c191472e2f66e71f8509f759f0468456a392e9b.png[/img]

[b]Taxes[/b]
Taxes are wealth based. At most once per day, a tax collector can and will collect taxes from each person, taking x% of the persons coins. The percentage is decided by the tax rate. All tax collectors will keep part of the taxes for themselves. Less honest tax collectors might keep more.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/17e17f09ddf0065012938f07564f3fa42b01d55a.png[/img]

[b]Distance popups[/b]
When selecting plots, various distance information is now shown.
If you select a home somebody owns, shows the distance to that person work.
If you select a workplace somebody owns, shows the distance to that persons home.
If you select a home nobody owns, shows the distance to all non occupied work plots.
If you select a workplace nobody owns, shows the distance to all non occupied home plots.
The text turns red if it is too far away to be eligible.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37768834/17e7d2b28fdeb78cab05ff7d0348c58d9676cf01.png[/img]

[b]Stability[/b]
Going public in June was equal parts exciting and terrifying. Some things went well and some not so well. All should now be well in the realm.

[b]Rebalanced values of items, plots and objects[/b]
With the upcoming tax collector the player will make money by taxing their citizens. Such a change prompted a rebalance, generally lowering numbers.

notes.title: Patch 0.1.2.x
notes.content:
[h1]Message from the developers[/h1]
Hello everyone and thank you for getting involved in this project!
We have been hard at work collecting information, both user reported/suggested and auto generated via diagnostics. There have been a few child sicknesses including one major blunder that affected the live version for a few hours Sunday afternoon GMT (deeply sorry about that, if your game crashed during that window odds are it was both completely unnecessary and one hundred percent my fault. I screwed the pooch).
As an avid player of these types of games ourselves we are familiar with the struggles these types of projects often face. With this message and accompanying patch notes we want to show you the level of transparency you can and should expect from us going into the future. 
Feel free to reach out and ask us anything, either here on Steam, the in game feedback menu which goes straight to my phone notifications, our Subreddit r/AGameofHumans, Facebook or directly at contact@scionstudios.
Thank you reading! None of this would be possible without people like you.


[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added support for various Screen modes (windowed, maximized windowed, fullscreen and exclusive fullscreen)
[*] Added support for toggling the game to run in background (e.g. tabbed out, not in focus) or to pause.
[*] Added support for vertical sync (be warned that some machines appear to stutter due to this, we have contacted Unity support over this issue).
[*] Added support for toggling Screen Space Ray Tracing on and off (greatly improved contact shadows and light bleeding at the cost of performance).
[*] Added the cost to destroy a plot to the plot inspector.
[*] Added the cost to construct a house to the plot inspector.
[*] Split the plot inspectors into different objects instead of a general one, allowing for the display of only the information relevant to the specific plot.
[/list]

[h2]General[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added version number to the main menu.
[*] New builds will automatically increment the version number.
[*] Characters will now spawn with a wider range of coins, some will be wealthier than others.
[*] Prayers now only add faith equal to the missing % of spiritual need instead of a flat value.
[*] Characters now prioritize socializing with other characters with a low social need (previously everyone would attempt to talk to popular people, e.g. attractive happy people, rendering them incapable of performing work due to their sheer popularity).
[/list]

[h2]Maps[/h2]
[list]
[*] Altered the Berghfoot map generation settings so that it is unlikely to generate a long, unassailable ridge which the intelligent characters of the world does not take into account when they decide how close they are to a potential berry bush.
[*] Tip: If you want to make your own maps before official tools exist, head over into "Steam/steamapps/common/A Game of Humans/AGameofHumans_Data/StreamingAssets/Maps", duplicate and rename one of the existing files and get to editing. As it is not a user friendly format but a computer generated one you will need to be very carefully follow how the files look but as they are very small it should hopefully not be too difficult :)
[/list]

[h2]Diagnostics[/h2]
[list]
[*] Improved diagnostics tools resulting in better auto-generated crash reports.
[*] Sending a bug report through the feedback menu will now automatically include all relevant system information.
[*] Added a bunch of diagnostic hooks into various processes to catch previously unfound errors (most notably in the save & load process)
[/list]

[h2]Localization[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added localization for crops
[/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Reverted from DX12 to DX11 as testing seems to have verified that a majority of the crashes simply vanished with this change. We are in contact with Unity support to see if the issue can be resolved (DX12 provides greater performance and as such we would prefer to use it)
[*] Changing the in game language should no longer cause AutoSave and QuickSave to crash upon their activation (even changing from English to English caused this).
[*] Music should no longer change track upon tabbing in and out if run in background is disabled.
[*] Attempting to add coins to an entity that ceased to exist during the process will now default the coins to the player instead (death taxes yay).
[*] Fixed an issue with items attached to a character and animations fading between each other causing an out of bounds index and thus a crash.
[*] Fixed an issue where the wrong character would be paid for the sale of a wood log.
[*] Fixed an issue where saving during an ongoing construction process could cause a crash.
[*] Fixed an issue where items placed in objects could cause a crash if multiple characters accessed the object at the same time.
[*] Deleting a house plot before the immigrant heading towards it reached it should no longer cause incorrect behavior.
[/list]


[h3]August
Scion Studios[/h3]
